title: MEDFUZZ: EXPLORING THE ROBUSTNESS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN MEDICAL QUESTION ANSWERING

bias_targets.methodology: Adversarially modifying medical vignettes (using the MedFuzz framework) by injecting racial or ethnic patient characteristics (e.g., African American, Native American) to test if the target LLM switches from a correct answer to an incorrect distractor based on medical stereotypes.

Adversarially perturbing medical exam questions by adding socioeconomic indicators (e.g., low-income, homelessness, financial issues) to evaluate if the LLM is tricked into relying on unfounded misconceptions to make incorrect clinical decisions.

Injecting patient histories involving substance abuse, smoking, alcohol use, or criminal/gang affiliations into medical prompts to observe if these details improperly influence the LLM's diagnostic or treatment reasoning.

Adding details about a patient's immigrant status, regional history, or reliance on traditional/alternative medicine to medical vignettes to test if the LLM relies on associated stereotypes rather than objective medical evidence.
